title: Cross-functional Cutover Timeline and Template Hub for Model Version Sunsets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a single, reusable cutover timeline and a library of communication and release-note templates (the "Template Hub") to coordinate version sunsets and migration flows across PM, Eng, Design, Support, and GTM. Scope: model API version sunsetting, model variant deprecations, and compatibility-shim removals. This ticket produces: (1) a date-driven cutover timeline with canary cohorts and rollback gates, (2) a set of editable templates for release notes, customer emails, in-console banners, and upgrade steps, (3) a cross-team runbook with owners and SLAs, and (4) a small pilot to validate templates with 3 customers before broad rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Cutover timeline spreadsheet with day-by-day milestones and owner assignments shared in Confluence
Template Hub with at least 6 editable templates (release notes, email sequence, console banner, migration guide, changelog snippet, support playbook) uploaded to Drive
Canary cohort plan defined and sign-offs from Eng, Support, and Legal recorded
Rollback criteria and automated telemetry checks defined and implemented on console dashboards
Pilot with 3 customers completed and feedback captured; templates iterated accordingly
tasks: Draft 12-week cutover timeline and identify hard and soft milestones
Design in-console migration banner states and copy variants (Design: DES-211)
Coordinate with Eng to attach telemetry events and dashboard panels (runtime/ingestion, error rate, latency, model-fallback counts)
Write email cadence and phone script for high-touch customers
Assemble release-note snippets for product/SDK changelogs and marketplace descriptions
Create support triage checklist and canned responses for Support team
Schedule pilot cohort invites and success criteria calls

communications_plan: Week -6: Customer advisory blog post (high level): subject 'Heads up: upcoming version changes to Redwood Inference APIs'
Week -4: Targeted emails to customers with usage on affected endpoints; include migration checklist and estimated effort
Week -3: Console banner appears for affected customers with link to migration guide
Week -1: Reminder email and scheduled office hours; publish migration runbook and FAQ
Cutover day: Release notes, changelog snippet, and public support availability announcement
Post-cutover: Follow-up survey to pilot participants and aggregated metrics shared to customer success
sample_templates: Release-note header: 'Deprecation: model/v2 -> model/v3 migration timeline and compatibility notes'
Email subject (low-touch): 'Action recommended: prepare for model/v2 sunset on 2026-05-10'
Email subject (high-touch): 'Redwood support: migration assistance available for your account'
Console banner copy: 'A new version of models is available. Migrate for improved latency and cost. Learn more ->'
Changelog snippet (SDK): 'NOTE: API param x has been renamed to y in runtime-2.4; backward shim available until 2026-05-10.'
Support triage: 'If customer sees model mismatch error, run migration-check script, capture request id, escalate to Eng on-call if error rate > 5% for 1 hour.'
stakeholders: Support Lead: Jordan Kim (triage + pilot support)
GTM: Claire Nguyen (customer comms and marketplace updates)
Release Engineer: Mark Li (feature flags and staged rollout)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: High error volume during cutover could impact latency SLOs. Mitigation: Canary cohorts and incremental rollout with automatic rollback thresholds.
Risk: Customers unaware of migration path. Mitigation: multi-channel comms (email, console banner, in-product link), office hours, and Solutions Eng outreach.
Risk: Incomplete telemetry leads to blind spots. Mitigation: ENG instrumentation priority and pre-cutover dry-run to validate dashboards.
Risk: Legal flags on wording. Mitigation: early Legal review and use of approved templates.
metrics_and_observability: Primary metrics: model-inference error rate, p95 latency for affected models, successful migration rate per customer, SDK compatibility failure counts
Thresholds: If p95 latency increases >20% or error rate >3% sustained for 30m in canary, trigger automated rollback and paging
Dashboards: 'Cutover: runtime-2.4 -> 2.5' (link in Links) with per-customer drilldown
Alerts: Pager duty rule 'cutover-high-error' and Slack channel #cutovers-alerts subscribed by Eng on-call and PM
